title: Paris Moulin Rouge Cabaret Show with Champagne Only or Dinner
description: Secure advance tickets to the historic Moulin Rouge to ensure your spot at an evening of song, dance, sensual costumes, and music in classic Parisian style. You’ll kick off the night with a glass of chilled Champagne, then watch a skilled troupe of 80 performers dance their way through the ‘Féerie’ show. Optional dinner upgrades add a multi-course meal of French cuisine, with a range of gourmet menus available.

reviews.usertext: The show is tremendous fun. Expect lines but they are orderly and almost all seats are good seats. 11pm show starts queuing at 10:30 and takes about an hour until everyone is seated. You can pre-arrange a taxi for 45 euros which might be worth it since you'll be getting out closer to 2 AM

Incredible visual spectacle. Several of the performers were Olympic caliber athletes. They displayed feats of strength with amazing grace and ease. My favorite part was the woman swimming in a clear tank filled with snakes. This show has been going strong for 130 years. This is a must do in Paris.

Note: men must wear trousers or they will make you purchase a used pair for 65 euro. At least we have a funny story to tell now ;)

The night starts with a 15 minute wait in a pretty long queue, but everything is inside and the wait doesnt feel very long. The hall itself looks amazing: very nice ambiance, dim lighting and good atmosphere. We had dinner, and the food was pretty good: the main advantage was getting there ealier, because people with dinner usually get seats closer to the stage. We ate our dinner with live music playing in the backround, and this part of the experience was overall pretty good. The people with a ticket without dinner made their way in right before the show started. Moving on, the show is what you pay for: it was simply AMAZING! The dancers were perfectly in sync, the stage was amazing (and with so many different back drops and decor), and the costumed were jaw-dropping. The show features quite alot of topless women, which is something you should know before going. So many plot twists, so many amazing costumes, and catchy songs. Overall, I’d say this is the best show I have ever seen. I would highly recommend, this was by far the best thing we saw in Paris. Unforgetable night.

I have deliberately waited a month to write my review as I wanted to see how I felt after time!

The positives! It's a bucket list thing for me to see a show at the Moulin Rouge so from that perspective I am happy I did it and really enjoyed the overall experience. The acrobatic acts were excellent and I loved seeing the cancan. The costumes were spectacular for the most part and the overall effects of some dances were brilliant. The individual sitting and idea of being on the tables as you would've been years ago was great, mostly.....

The negatives! You are really packed in, back to back and right next door to your neighbour. We were a two and our table was for 6, luckily another couple only was sat with us or it would've been unbearable. My seat backed the stage so I had to work in unison with the man behind me to turn my chair so I could see, that's how tight it was. If there was an emergency it would be incredibly difficult to get out safely from many parts of the show. We did have a good view. Some acts were just weird, two flying singers, a woman wrestling a snake in a pool and and an ill advised Asia themed dance and set. The singers were lip syncing and that was so obvious, the dancing was good but some were not great. You just expect live singing and a bit more complex dancing.

Overall it was a good night but it was expensive and I would say there are better shows out there, it needs updating and given some more life and it needs to be genuinely live performed. I'm glad I went, I'd say definitely go and experience it but don't expect your socks to be blown off.

TLDR: Your money is better spent elsewhere. The show could use some work. *Some spoilers below*

As a lover of the 2001 film, I was excited to see the origin of the Can-Can dance and Parisian entertainment. We were sadly left confused and baffled at the end of the night.

We were a group of 3 friends total who had purchased tickets online for the show + champagne weeks before. We arrived when they requested and waited in a long line to enter. We were finally escorted to a tiny table (6-top) in the back center, across from a couple with their teenage son. We were confused as we thought we would have our own table and could barely squeeze in between the other table that was crammed next to ours. When the waiter came over, one in our group swapped their champ for wine and the additional waitress that came over struggled to open the bottle, citing it was her first night on the job.

The show began and the elegant dancers emerged. The female dancers were all on point, but the male dancers were not as on point from the get go, and seemed like they could have used a few additional rehearsals.

The performers in between (roller bladers, acrobats, swimmer, dancers) were amazing and a true spectacle! However, the storyline overall was lacking and it felt outdated at times (I recall a weird jump from an Asian country to a 1940's jukebox). Could have dealt with less costume changes as well, but most were beautiful.

I know times are tough and they probably increased the ticket cost to stay open/pay staff accordingly, but I couldn't help but feel like we had wasted our money at times. And the Can-Can didn't even end the show... leaving two stars for the dancers and performers that delivered that night!

All in all, and without too much shade, you are better off spending that same money on a proper Cirque du Soleil show or elsewhere. Hope they can sharpen up the show for future iterations!

For the best in France, I was expecting a much better show. Being seated was okay, they were to get our complimentary champagne but some how forgot. We asked the server half way through the show, to which he brought but then wanted us to pay 90 euros. After explaining this, and a lot of fact checking they reluctantly gave us our included champagne. Now the show itself, I was expecting it to be great considering the reviews but The dancers were out of time to each other, sometimes even heading in the opposite direction to where they were meant to dance.
Disappointing, but still glad I went. Price is extremely overpriced.

If you want covid then this is the place to go!

€250 to go to this show to be cramped in a theatre with 100’s of people. We were sat in the middle of our section with two others on our table. To the back of us were four others on either side. We couldn’t even rest back on our chair they were that close. Zero social distancing. There’s a reason why they don’t let you choose your seat as if you saw the seating plan before you went you wouldn’t go.

Ok show but not worth the risk of covid.

I can explain how disappointing this experience was tonight. The dancing was very poor, uncoordinated and the show was literally partially naked women walking around the stage. The only thing that made us not leave mid performance were the acrobatic performances (3 in total), however this is not worth the high ticket price for no singing (they barely put an effort to show its playback), no dancing and just nudity.
I thought this would be a cabaret show and true to the moulin rouge history however this is ver very poor. I would not advise this at all! Save your money for other parisien experiences

We couldn’t go due to France not allowing British tourists in the country and even though on the get your guide website said free cancellation up to 24 hours before. We were told no refund would be given which is false advertising. If it isn’t free cancellation this need to be removed from the website

My daughter, 9, loves all things singing and dancing so I tried to book tickets before our trip but understandably it was booked out. Lou, in customer services advised to check each morning at 10 and 4 pm for cancellations. I did last evening and was able to secure a last minute booking! We arrived early for 9 pm show, no queuing. We got our own table at the back up a small set of steps with a good view of the stage. My girls were mesmerised by the dancers, the crystals, the feathers, the lights! Not only were there dancers - there were strong men, skaters, snakes, aerial scene across the crowd. For me the best part was seeing how excited my children were. My 6 yr old daughter fell asleep towards the end (to be fair it was a long night for her). It definitely was a core memory for my eldest. And my husband and I enjoyed it too. I deducted one point as it is expensive but I’m glad we went.

Personally I have seen the show many times, I keep returning to take friends and they are always incredibly impressed saying this is the best part of our visit to Paris.

I pre-purchased tickets online for the 4 of us at around 83 euros per person, basic tickets without meals or drinks and we chose the 9pm show.

A 2 minute queue on arrival and 5 minute queue inside to be shown our seats, we were sat adjacent to the stage so close that the feathers on the dancers outfits often brushed my head which was not a problem, certainly unrestricted views.

The dancers as always were a treat, the costumes an amazing spectacle the supporting acts of the strongmen, roller dancers and contortionist really amazing.

The ponies on the stage and boa constrictors in the pool are always great to watch.

The staff at the Moulin Rouge are ALL lovely from the coat storage to the waiters, the entrance staff and everyone else you encounter are friendly, super efficient and welcoming.

I will continue to introduce friends to this piece of Paris History and a great night out.

The evening at the Moulin Rouge was definitely a highlight of our Paris trip.

We got there early and sat close to the stage which was great to see a lot.

The costumes and the stage show were awesome. The dancers did a great job and the solo acts also really impressed us.

We would have liked a little more information about the dress code, some came in full suits and others in t-shirts and jeans. Also, I would recommend drinking a little more than just buying champagne, it's very warm in the room.

All in all: we would go back to the show anytime, it's definitely worth the money!!

I would actually rather give 4.5 stars instead of 4 but half rating can't be selected. Magical evening, a must do once in your life. Moulin Rouge is not half naked ladies dancing around, it's a beautiful and enchanting spectacle that will lighten your night, following a story arc and enthrall your evening. The food is sublime and if you don't like the bubbly version, you can opt for red, white wine or 2 of any drinks in the menu. The show is simply divine, the only draw back is that you might be seated on a table a 6, even though you are 2, and have 4 other people lurking at your food while your eating.

We were wedged six to a table that was only big enough for four drinking lousy champagne after waiting for an hour in line when the show started late.

The singing/dancing was good, costumes amazing but the circus like acts (which I didn’t expect) actually stole the show. I would go again but I don’t regret the experience.

Overall this is an enjoyable night but the organisation in the MR is non existent ! We were booked for 11pm show & joined the queue about 10.15 pm but didn’t get to our seat under 11pm & there were many people behind us ! There appeared to be no organisation to the table seating & we were sat with 2 other couples at a table of 6 which was fine but there was v v limited space to move. The show then didn’t start till after 11.30 & they were still seating people.. complete chaos & also meant we weren’t out till almost 2am ! The acts were good & were very entertaining but I somehow thought it would have been more professional as it’s the moulin rouge after all & the tickets are v expensive. You do get some champagne in with the ticket price but it isn’t great quality however I think you can switch for wine . There is also a ‘no photos’ rule but we had people taking photos & videos in front of us with nothing said - quite annoying to have a mobile phone constantly taking pictures. Overall it was a really enjoyable night but the chaos getting in & getting seated was a joke.

Great production and the talent portions of the show were amazing. The dancing was mediocre. We queued for over an hour to be seated after arriving well before the start time. The tickets were for 11pm but we were not seated until midnight by which point they had decided to start the show without numerous customers being seated.

The show started late and there was a long queue in a very warm holding area. However, it was completely worth it. The venue is gorgeous and the performers were incredible. We didn’t know what to expect, but it was one of the most mesmerising spectacles we have ever seen. Strongly recommended for anyone visiting Paris!

The energy and colour of this show is breathtaking. The dancers and singers are amazing as are the costumes.
However, there is one segment of the show that includes pythons swimming in a tank of water which I didn't like at all. As an animal advocate this type of performance is totally unnecessary and a let down to the overall experience.
Tip on transport: if using a train to get to the Moulin Rouge check your return line doesn't close after a certain time. We were left feeling vulnerable not knowing how to get back to our hotel having to ask for assistance on an alternate way back to our hotel as a mugging was taking place a few metres from us.

This show was much better than expected. It was very beautiful, but also very exciting at times. We were very close to the stage, as literally, death defying acts were being performed.
My husband was reluctant to go on this adventure, & afterwards he said he would highly recommend it to any of our friends.

Ah, that moment you realize: The sidebar attractions, designed to allow the main dancers to get ready for their next set, are way more entertaining than the Moulin Rouge show itself. Yikes! You could feel the energy lift when those 'filler' entertainers took the stage. I do understand that the Moulin Rouge show is nodding it's head to the past- I get it- but sets/skits were borderline cheesy. Beautiful costumes and dancers, but that is not enough to warrant the cost and horrific seating. It's not the table sharing, six per on our upper level, it's the table angle and lack of view as a result. I also understand dinner theatre seating is different than a cinema. The issue is the grab for dollars and packing in too many. Literally could not cross/uncross legs for fear of hitting the table and spilling champagne. As the show dragged on, we were more and more uncomfortable trying to sit perfectly rigid and hold our heads 'just so' in order to see. We didn't hate it, but we sure didn't love it. Save your money for a better show like Cirque du Soleil.

This was a wonderful experience. My son and I enjoyed the food and the show. We had a great time and had lots of laughs with the people sitting beside us. The costumes were beautiful. The dancers and singers were very good. The entertainment during dinner was also good. I would definitely get there by 6:30. It worked well for us for a Sunday night. Book now. We met some people in Paris that wanted to see the show. All shows were sold out during their entire stay in Paris.

The dancers and other performers were excellent. The seating was shockingly poor. We were a party of 3, made to share with another couple. The table was side on to the stage so we did not have a full view of the performers. The seats were so tightly packed together no one could get in or out or move in their seats. It was uncomfortable and definitely did not reflect the price we paid.

It was my birthday celebration last year and definitely a highlight of our Paris trip!

We booked the dinner and show option that started at 7pm. We were seated with several other people in a table but that did not bother us, the couple beside us were friendly but we did not talk that much, we were seated at the corner table giving us a good view of the front stage. While having dinner we were serenaded by a couple of singers and a band who performed both in English and French. I know this was not the Feerie show but I enjoyed this dinner entertainment so much as well. The dinner came as starter, main course, then dessert. It came with half a bottle of champagne to share per couple. The dinner tastes ok (not great) but presented very well. I've had better meals in other restaurants in Paris. But the champagne I had here was so good I keep on reminiscing about it. The servers are pretty quick but they get busy serving a lot of tables it is hard to call their attention sometimes.

Coming to the Feerie show after the dinner, I did not expect there is a hidden stage right beside me, it suddenly popped up when the show was about to start. The show was in French, while on queue by the reception they offered english translation booklets - but why read when you can just enjoy watching them sing and dance.

This is probably my first time watching a cabaret style show and I truly enjoyed it. Definitely recommend booking the dinner and show option for a fuller experience. (Of course when it is safe to do so).

I went last year in October 2019 (the option is giving me till November 2019 only).

As expected and hoped for. An amazing night at this famous location. We booked for dinner and the show and weee not left disappointed. The food was lovely, all 3 courses and a bottle of champagne included. The staff were friendly and attentive. We were so lucky we had a table right next to the stage. We recommend you arrive early. We got there at 6.15 for the 7pm dinner and we were in the first 10 people in the queue. Get there early to get the best tables it’s worth it. The show was fantastic. Thank you Moulin Rouge. A dream come true.

Whilst the show was faultless, we found the seating was totally unacceptable. We were packed in far too closely, you literally could not move, not only was this uncomfortable ( we booked as a couple and ended up sitting on a table of 10!).
The most concerning thing about the seating was it was a total fire hazard.

During the show staff were collecting money off customers who had purchased extra drinks.

Myself and my friend were at the moulin rouge show on monday.
We both paid £179 each for our ticket which included the meal.

To start our meal was not nice, The tuna and asparagus were freezing and had obviously been prepared hours before.
The chicken we both did not eat it was tough and tasteless and the dessert was rock solid.

We had to leave the show early due to feeling uncomfortable by male staff.
(Mohammad) our server was accommodating to begin with and offered us free drinks and even moved us seats to vip and from there everything went wrong and we were made to feel very uncomfortable and he asked us what our hotel was called and also told us we couldn’t order another drink and we were told to slow down drinking.
He asked my friend if her hotel room had room for two and other waiters were watching us.

we left the show early and had to wait until Mohammad left to run to the toilet and try and leave. We felt extremely unsafe and as two females it was scary.

The show itself was amazing for what we saw but food and staff I have to fault I am not happy.

It was a lot of fun and super kitschy. My favorite acts where the acrobatic interludes. And the costuming was amazing. We had great seats but the theater is really packed in and then they rush you out at the end because performances are back to back.

The food was ok. But not really worth what we paid for it…however the service was excellent. Our waiters were friendly and efficient. The champagne was delivered promptly and the pre show act created a great atmosphere. The show itself was fabulous…and having the specialty acts between sets added to the enjoyment. The overall production was full of energy and was very well executed. Costumes were lovely and the dancing was great. Thoroughly recommend this to anyone wanting a “special” experience

Awful. Just awful. This cabaret is stuck in the 70s and 80s. They jam you in like sardines, the costumes are great to look At but the music, feel and performance is just so out of date.
The strong men and the roller skaters were highlights but seemed to be after thoughts in a bid to modernise.
The whole snake scene was just abhorrent and don’t get me started on the clowns.
Utterly disappointed- champagne was the only thing that saved me

Performers, stage props, lighting music made a superb show worth a watch. Waiting time of over one hour was tedious. And the late night show means we missed the metro ride back. Earlier time booking would have been better

It was a nice show so but definitely overpriced given the sitting arrangement given to us it could have been far better with Pre assigned seats and reducing the audience per show by 70%, it was very cramped. On the brighter side it was colorful and nice dance performances. Nudity was unnecessary.

We were seated directly in front of the stage with our backs to the show. It was literally impossible to watch the show! We asked to move but we’re refused. It was a complete rip off. All we had a view of was the room full of other customers watching the show.

We didn't get to do the dinner as it was already booked up a week in advance so we did the Champagne early show. We were let in early (8 pm) and since we were a family of four, we had a table to ourselves. We had a great view of the stage. We were a bit nervous about the dress code since we had travelled from overseas and had only packed athletic shoes for walking but it was not an issue at all, perhaps because the girls were wearing dresses so at least had made an effort. In case you were expecting the show to be similar to the movie, it is not the same songs or storyline. The songs are in French and even though we don't speak the language, it did not detract from the performance. The costumes were beautiful, as were the dancers, and the acrobats/special performers were absolutely incredible. What those acrobats were able to do was extraordinary. Truly death defying and my jaw was on the floor. Thoroughly enjoyed it

Definitely expensive but so worth it .
A very bizarre experience and not what we expected. Very fast paced not stop entertainment with multiple dances and specialist acts. Credit to the dancers as there are a lot of costume changes . No specific theme but felt a bit like 70’s cabaret in part or a holiday park show . Something you absolutely have to experience at least once in your life although I wouldn’t take anyone under 16 as there is a lot of topless dancing ,It is however tasteful and not crude or offensive . Be aware though you are quite tightly packed in and we shared a table with another couple on a table that seated up to 6. Drinks are reasonably priced but not cheap . Your paying for an experience and I certainly won’t forget it, a very positive memory for us and our time in Paris .

This competes with the Eiffel for the highlight of our Paris trip. You walk in and are drawn in by the color of the theater, the soft lighting. You truly are drawn back into history. The show is indulgent with music, great costumes, and light. And it doesn't matter if you don't speak French, just enjoy the show. A few musical numbers, mixed in with an acrobatic feat. Just amazing! If you've ever seen the Copacabana show in Havana, this is just like it, but better. Tip: Plan for getting home if you are at the late show, the subways will be closed after the performance.

For the vast majority of the performance, bare-breasted women parade around the stage while fully dressed men move around them. There were a few acrobatic acts to break up the topless parading that were impressive in the skill required, but not particularly interesting. I cannot understand any of the positive reviews.

The show was a unique experience. Talented cast, fabulous set and costumes with the addition of incredible circus style acts in between sets. There was one with snakes so if you don’t like them be prepared. We were on the champagne show. We were packed very tightly in at tables bolted to the floor. I’m a UK size 10 and struggled to get into my seat & with a large gentleman behind me I was definitely squashed. Each quest had a half bottle of delicious champagne but if you wanted to purchase an alternative ( we tried beer and water ) it never arrived. The show lasted under two hours without an interval so there was no opportunity to chase this up.

Great entertainment and not a bad champagne either, half a bottle each is plenty. Thought it good value for money considering it’s one of the must do shows. The main show was spectacular although the live snakes is something they could definitely do without and the warm up act was terrible, they looked half asleep and bored rigid

9pm show with bottle of champagne between two.
I have seen this show half a dozen times over the past 30 years and it never fails to delight.
Yes, it is quite cramped in there and you can get very warm.
Take your coat in with you as it's mayhem queuing to get it back from the kiosk after the show.
However, the show is spectacular overall, vibrant and beautiful.
I personally would not go for the dinner prior to the show but just once in a lifetime for visitors who live on the other side of the world, the experience and expense would be worth it.
Useful tip: if you don't drink champagne, you can choose something else for the value of your share.
I took half a bottle of champagne, my friend had 2 gin and tonics.
The moulin rouge is only 1 minute walk from Blanche metro station.

Very well organised show, and a real experience. We had the 9pm champagne tickets, and were seated quickly on arrival at a table with two other friendly couples. The champagne arrived quickly and then the show started. You don’t purchase other drinks incidentally, and so there’s no waiter service as such.
The show itself is really good, with the cabaret telling a story of the Moulin Rouge through the years, and they also had three special acrobat acts that were amazing. For the show, I did feel we wanted to see more of the traditional Can-Can dancing with the music that it’s famous for as there was probably no more than a minute of that in the whole evening, but the rest was really good. And yes, it’s topless throughout, but you do genuinely forget that after the first few minutes and for the most part there are discrete and tasteful mesh, fishnet, tassels and so on providing a very tiny bit of modesty

A fantastic show on a par with any Las Vegas show or Cirque de Soleil. Thrilling feats of strength, perfect high speed roller skating and eben a massive snake filled water tank that rose from beneath the floor with a woman who swam with the snakes. Increfibly beautiful women and men in million dlllar costumes! Wow! Don't miss this.

This was an amazing show. Very energetic and fun. We had the Champagne service, and truly enjoyed that part as well. You have the main event group numbers that were super entertaining, but also some nice "in between" acts that are incredibly talented acts as well.

Oh my… what a disappointment. I’m a huge fan of shows and I have been anywhere from Broadway to Pantages and Las Vegas. This was like a high school musical gone wrong. The vocals were lip synced. The dancers were out of sync. The only thing worth it was the solo shows in between. No storyline. No smooth transitions. Terrible! A waste of time and money. Way overpriced for what I got! At some point, the dancers held flashlights to their faces for lighting. Really? Can’t you update the lighting a bit?
If there was at least some synchronization between the dancers maybe it would be a smoother experience. I wouldn’t recommend. I am so sorry for this. And it was the one thing I didn’t want to miss in Paris

The dancers were talented but overall it was tacky and badly directed. I would also like to mention that one act used snakes in a pool that a dancer dived into. The snakes were visibly trying to swim away from the dancer as she pulled them down and tried to get them to swim around her. It was unpleasant to watch and had I known they use real animals in the act I would not have gone.

First of all, we had front row seats right next to the stage. We could see and feel every expression, body movement and muscle of every performer. The entire experience was jaw dropping, breathtaking and proof that there is a God. The talent these performers possess is short of a miracle. The entire show was spectacular but hands down, my favorite act was the male and female dance act from the song Rise Up by Andra Day. One of the few songs played in English, which I appreciated as an American. The performance left me in tears.

Very outdated, felt like I stepped into the past where women subject themselves to crap dancing topless, animal abuse… bad miming and dancing was nothing special.

The men were mostly covered but the women were exposed continuously. Very cringeworthy.

The only appearances I enjoyed where there was actual talent were the people that came on and did acrobatics, that was very cool but was overshadowed by more topless women jumping up and down after.

Very disappointing.

The room is beautiful and you can feel old Paris exuding from your surroundings! The waiter was really entertaining and made it even more fun too. The dancers are gorgeous and the other performers were impressive as well. I really loved seeing the beautiful bodies and smiles of the dancers as they danced (they kick so high!) the night away!

Awful. Dancers were not coordinated, costumes were cheap and the entire show was confusing. Topless women being chased by clowns? The show is not sexy or interesting. The balancing act was okay and offers a 5 minute respite from an otherwise theatrical dumpster fire. Save your money.

Excellent show. Apart from a very exquisite dance show with luxurious outfits and great coreography, the performance shows of various acrobats were amazing.
The menu was tasty, quality food and chapagne was quite good.
A very nice experience and for sure it'll be on the "to do list" every time we'll be in Paris.
I reccomend to book the tickets from their own webpage as only there you have all ticket option available.

The show wasn't a tight as we have previously seen before covid and dancing looked sloppy. Overall still a good show. We were crammed onto a tiny table for two that had been put onto a stairway to squeeze in extra seats which made you feel constantly in the way. This appeared greedy as the right hand view of the stage was obstructed. At over £100 per ticket this wasn't brilliant.

The dinner was not that good. The chocolate mousse was wonderful. The band that played only played American, English music and I was disappointed that it wasn't french music. And there is two hours between the dinner and Moulin Rouge cabaret show. That's a lot of time. The show itself was excellent! Loved the dancers, and the acts. They all work so hard! Just incredible! I was sad when it was over! What a great experience!

I have to admit, I thought this thing would be a tourist trap and a waste of money, due to the movie. However, my wife wanted to go so I had no choice. 😊. I am sure glad we did, because the dancing, the choreography, the amazing outfits, and the great stunts made this show eye popping! We paid around $130 with champagne included, and it was worth that price.
Great show! It was like Disneyland for adults.

Overall it was really good however the guys looked as if they had been plucked from the audience and told to dance. They did their best but it was painful to watch at times. The singers did a lovely miming job. A bit like seeing Justin Bieber on tour. The ‘story’ got a bit bizarre as it was a walk through time in one segment but it was all over the place. I was so confused I lost the plot. The costumes went from wow to why? The acrobatics were amazing and were the highlight for us. Be warned live animals are part of the act which we didn’t know in advance. Can the girls doing the can can scream a bit as that would have made brilliant finale. In a nutshell - worth it but it is like prospecting for gold. A few nuggets and some needs re-thinking.

Three only reason it’s a four was the seating.
E were placed on the side and missed some of three incredible show that is performed in there center of the rotunda of three theater.
The artists were outstanding. The performances were choreographed so well and the stage settings and backdrops excellent.
Although there is some nudity,tastefully done, bravo for the French!
The champagne was plentiful and service was good. Celebrated with our offspring of adult age and thoroughly enjoyed by all.

I have no words to explain how beautiful and fantastic it was! I truly recommend! Our option was only with champagne, and I think it was the greatest choice, because during the show o couldn’t blink my eyes how impressed I was with the spectacular! The line was okay, there are lines everywhere in Paris, so it took us around 40 minutes. We got a great spot in the front and the staff was very polite and friendly. I’ll never forget that day!

Now I know where Vegas got their show idea from. Dancers were beautiful, other acts were fantastic. Only complaint was we got in line at 10:35, stood and waited until 11:10 when we were seated then show finally started @11:30 though it did finish @1:15. Taxi was ridiculously overpriced so we walked back to our hotel

It was “okay”. The ambience is great, just as you’d imagine, 70s lounge singers crooning whilst you wait for the show to start, red veiled lamps on tables, white suited waiters, people dressed up. But the show is “okay”. The speciality acts are the best parts by a margin, the singing and dancing is super impressive in terms of costumes and singing, but the dancing and choreography which make up the majority is more patchy…. If you’ve grown up seeing professional dance troupes on TV talent shows, you might be scratching your head at the level of coordination and technique. But maybe that’s not the point. And final point, I know they’ve got work to timed slots, but the end of the show makes you feel very processed - lights up on final dance, then glasses and tables being cleared almost instantaneously ready for the next show.

Moulin rouge was a great ambiance and performance. There was just one very sad point, there is one part of the show with snakes under water and you can definitely see that they struggle trying to escape / breathe which is very sad. I think the dancers are good enough by themselves without the need of bringing this kind of extra. Otherwise, all good.

My husband and I reserved the show with champagne. We were there 45 minutes before the 9:00PM show. We got in very quick and were sitted promptly. The show was very entertaining, the music, dancers, costumes and the singers were great! We are used to seeing shows in US so I can't say is the best I have seen but definetly a Paris experience.

Moulin rouge is very intensiv and intersting show. From entrance you can see that somethin special is going on. Show keeps your brain ocupied all the time. You can feel the history and imagine how was it in the past.
My recommandation!

The show is genuinely fantastic. Very impressive performance. Great champagne. Only down side was the efficiency of entrance. Told to arrive for 10:30 for the 11pm show (fine) however we didn't get let in until 11:10 and they were seating people until 1130pm. Queuing for 40 minutes wasn't great. But once inside I cannot stress how fantastic it was. Well worth a visit.

It was a great show but not sure it was worth the price of admission. Great detail was given about the dress code but no body appeared to follow it. There were sports shoes and sandals aplenty.
Having said that it was colourful and well choreographed.
Be advised to ensure that you check transport for your return trip to your hotel if you are doing the 11pm show. As some metro and bus services are not available.

Everyone suggested we see Moulin Rouge on our 1st Paris trip. The show choreography was as dated as the costumes. Lip-syncing too? Please let the young dancers do a more new-age show with fresh young costumes, maybe some dazzling lighting and without snakes. And real spot lighting for the floating man vs. handheld flashlight. Come on guys it's 2020, it's only fair that the men should show as much skin as the women. The men had clothes from head to toe to wrist. Go to Vegas and see how it's done!

Long queues in the exceptionally hot weather. We arrived early but still had a long time to queue and go up and
down several flights of stairs before queuing again inside after security. It was a relief to be shown to our seats in the cool.

Typical Parisian show with the French Cancan famous dance which is an iconic image of the Paris by night. The dinner is a standard one, with good food that you get from a menu. The waiters are running every where ass the show must go on. Superb evening.

This was the best show that we have ever seen, from start to finish the production was faultless, the dancers were stunning, and the acrobatics were mind blowing, one act was a lady who could bend her body, well she must be made of rubber, absolutely astonishing, all acts were equally fantastic, this is one show everyone should see.
We had the Champagne tickets, but next year we are going to have the dinner and show, it looked fantastic. Highly recommended, see you soon.

It’s really a great show. Yes, some (not all) of the dancers are topless. But, it’s an entire show. You really forget about the partial nudity when watching the incredible dancing. Then in between acts there are performances by jugglers, contortionists, strength, etc. it was definitely a great experience. I would see it again.

I am sure the show was very innovative when it was created in the late 19th century, but today it is an average show. if you have been exposed to shows like Cirque du Soleil, a Disney or Broadway show, you will not be impressed. However, it is something to do if you are in Paris so you can say that you saw it.

From the bad reviews, I didn't expect much, but the show was FENOMENAL. I haven't seen anything like this. The show is unique and there is a reason that this is the most famous cabaret in the world. The saporting acts are FABILOUS, I can't describe them you have to see it. I would't think twice to go again !!!
Must see !

We had the pre-dinner followed by the show. Good seats close to the stage.

Queuing, seating and service was smooth. The food was average by French standards, but OK.

The show was as expected with some impressive gymnastic acts and a surprise pool-based number. The cabaret dancing as seen on TV.

The dress code is relaxed, just avoid shorts and flip flops.

Our 1st night in Paris will never be forgotten after we took in this FABULOUS SHOW! I didn't know what to expect except Can-Can Girls The show was so much more. We went to a 9pm show (we had dinner prior, just across the street at Rouge Bis 4.5 Stars!). The show was non-stop for 1 hour 45 minutes. A fantastical mixture of amazing acts, dancing, music, costumes, all World Class. Don't miss this!

Great fun night out in Paris. It’s the original burlesque show where the can can was invented. Although the show is a few numbers to long in our opinion, we thought it was a Great night out. PS.. the reviews that complain about the dress code are ridiculous. It CLEARLY a states on your tickets the dress code. Don’t be THAT American.. plz

Must see show! We got there at 10:15pm for the 11pm show and the line was really long by 11:30pm. We were towards to front of the line and got great seats, basically in front of the stage. It is an absolute must see while in Paris, the set design and costumes are incredible! My boyfriend and I had the best time!! We will go again when we’re in Paris next :)

If you want to get a great experience DO NOT go there. Starting with a very uncomfortable place you could find great places in Paris despite this. The weather inside was insane. No air condiciones. The show is really old fashion. Very old. And boring. I don’t recommend spend any penny on them

A fabulous show, amazing costumes the speciality acts were spell binding.
However you are squashed like sardines at a table that would comfortably sit four has six, once in there no moving you are literally shoulder to shoulder. As you are sat sideways to the stage you have to twist but no room to twist whole body so not good for back sufferers, I’m a size 12 so not sure how larger people manage and definitely not for pregnant women.
Not sure whether France has the same health and safety as England re capacity but if there was an emergency we wouldn’t have got out quickly.

We both really enjoyed the show and would highly recommend it. It was amazing, all the different acts and costume changes it was all just brilliant. My only negative is that if u are a couple u will likely be put on a table with others u don’t know and it is a bit cramped and also for some reason air conditioning comes on just before the show and if u are sitting by it then it does get cold. All that aside it’s worth every penny.

So enjoy our visit to Moulin Rouge - go there every time we're in Paris.
Simply put 'Joie de vie' (the Joy of Life) is all there in these amazing performers and atmosphere. (Me, my daughter and my granddaughter)
Caroline Smith

It’s the Moulin Rouge you have to go but I would 100% skip the dinner portion. I had not had a bad meal in Paris until I ate here. The show is the show, come with realistic expectations and a good attitude and I’m sure you will enjoy it.

The show was amazing but my biggest complaint is the fact we were crammed in. Even the waiters struggled to get to the tables, my chair was knocked on numerous occasions. The food was ok, mass produced but ok.

No free cancellation. I made a mistake with the date of the booking and wanted to cancel a week in advance but they were too rigid. Would have saved a lot more money if I just waited and bought in person. The problem is I didn’t notice the date and it was showing next month as the experience was quite booked up. Ended up not seeing moulin rouge at all w all that money wasted.

What a way to celebrate my birthday, although it might have been more of a gift for my husband than me haha! Such a great show, so tastefully done and professional. We loved the entire show! If you WANT to be up in front select the option of dinner before the show, that is where those people were all seated. Be aware, they sit you next to each other and not across from each other so that one person from the party gets the front seat at the table. Which is appropriate, I think! Great show, unforgettable!

Was always on my bucket list. Did not disappoint! Was very much worth it! We arrived at 8:54 pm, was immediately seated for the 9 pm show with great seats. My attention was kept throughout the whole performance. Get your tickets now!

The show was good, but seating was terrible too cramped. The shop was closed so I couldn’t get perfume and tan I wanted to purchase. I tried booking dinner but it sold out while booking. We had 8 pm show with champagne. Next time I would only book with dinner. Or else I feel like it wasn’t worth the price.

My husband and I went to Moulin Rouge for the 11 pm show on Friday. It was definitely worth it! We were not sure what to expect but it was SO much more than what we expected. It was beautiful costumes, dancing, and music. There were also different performers/acts showcased which were incredible. We did not have drinks or eat there so I can not speak for that. We both really enjoyed the show and were glad we made it apart of our trip to Paris!

Two adult daughters and their mother on a birthday night at Moulin Rogue. After reading the reviews we didn't have high expectations and it ended up being brilliant. Lots of fun, the costumes were amazing and a nice variety of song/dance/acts. Well worth the money.

The show is generally good! Maybe more a mixt modern dance then a cabaret show.is probably that type of experience that you do it once and never repeat it.
If you are on a budget trip not recommended because of the value for money report.
The place itself is very nicely done

Fun time! Champagne was nice. People dressed in a variety of clothes so don’t get too worried about what you’ve packed, just put your best foot forward and plan to have a fun time watching a show with different themes. This is not for the conservative!!

highly overrated lots of money for dinner and show Vegas does a better job save your money. it is an experience that robs your wallet. Food is subpar and not worth it. We came we saw and others do it better

I went on my own, had a nice bottle of champagne and was sat right at the front. Made some friends next to me, dancers were extremely talented- definitely will be returning. I can see how this is art. At first I was blushing but then the admiration for the talent & beauty came shortly after. Bringing my other half next time.

We attended Moulin Rouge on Friday 13th of May and it was fantastic. The variety provided throughout the night was superb! We had a great seat with two bottles of Champagne provided. A bit cramped across the whole venue but worth the visit.

What an amazing experience! From arrival at the Moulin Rouge looking spectacularly beautiful outside and equally beautiful inside. We had opted to dine with a bottle of champagne and we had no regrets. The food service was first class and the show was spectacular and unique. We absolutely loved it.

A "must do" experience. My first time at a Cabaret. Yes, it's a LOT of money, but it was a fantastic evening. Seating was a little cramped for some (though we got lucky).
The rollerskaters and other acts were amazing. There was more nudity than I was expecting (I only expected the occasional glimpse!), so if that's a problem for you, be warned. A very slick show.

Such a waste of Money, it was same level of entertainment team at hotel. Very crowded. On their website it says it suitable for age 6+ , seriously??? Expensive and really not worth the price. Also the area near by is very poor you will not find a nice place to sit for a drink or dinner. We went with 3 boys, we had to go and buy long trousers for them . Had to buy at souvenir shop.

Would always recommend seeing this famous show once but would not return. The tables are too close together and the angle means it’s difficult for both of you to have a great view. We choose the better menu with Champagne and glad we did. The show and the drinks are over priced but would still recommend to see. Some of the dancing wasn’t great at the beginning but the acts are amazing.

I was advised by a friend that Moulin Rouge was the best cabaret in Paris .. and boy was he right !!
I was blown away by the magnificent costumes, the sets,the speciality acts and the wonderful dancers. Pricey? .. yes ,but you can see where the money goes . An evening I shall never forget .. Magnifique !

We were part of a tour and would never have picked the Moulin Rouge show if on our own. The show was great, food was not bad, wine & champagne good. I did not know what to expect but the show exceeded anything I could have come up with.

What an incredible experience! An amazing show from start to finish. Unbelievable acts between the dance sets which made you hold your breath. A modern twist to the Can Can.
Friendly waiter service. Lovely champagne. And the majority of people were dressed up looking fabulous!

My wife and I got the tickets with the bottle of champagne with the first show. It was a lot of money and I hoped it was worth it. It was! It was 2 hours of non stop over the top entertainment! Just incredible! We loved it! They do a fine job and I really don't have the ability to express how good the show was.

Finally, the third time in Paris, I have been able to see Moulin Rouge show! Fantastic production and entertainment. My husband and I had a fantastic time. I The service was professional and friendly. We opted for thé champagne only, no dinner as there are so many restaurant options in Montmarte!

On spite of previous reviews, I can honestly say my friend and I were impressed. The costumes, the energy, the total performance was exceptional.
We had the champagne only option and in truth expected a glass not a bottle. I expected something like vinegar and was pleasantly surprised.
I would ho again.

Best activity with 2 teenagers on our five day trip to Paris. Great show with beautiful costumes and some great dancers. Wonderful gymnasts (and roller skaters) made the evening even better. I highly recommend.

All I can say is WOW! Was worried that it would be a tourist trap , quite the opposite. Enter the Moulin Rouge and experience the high-class timeless cabaret experience. Dazzling costumes , outstanding performances that left my jaw all the way on the floor. A few surprises I won’t spoil … perfect for honeymoon , girls night , bachelorette party.
Great environment, service, food & drink. The show was absolutely fantastic well worth it. If you plan to visit Paris you must see the moulin rouge cabaret show....outstanding.
Best evening ever. Lovely food and drink, highly professional service and an excellent view of an excellent show. I cannot rate this high enough. I loved every minute.

Moulin Rouge is a must see and experience you that has to be on your Paris Itinerary! Almost all seating in the theater is in good view and you are randomly seated. The earlier you arrive I think the better your chance is off getting to be placed in better areas even though all are pretty good. highly recommended!!!

Always wanted to visit Moulin Rouge show and it was a fabulous show. Atmosphere was great and the acts were amazing. My husband did find it a tight squeeze as the seats were very cozy. It's worth check seating but we had excellent view.
I did remind the shop assistant selling keepsakes to be more pleasant as she did act as if she was superior to customers. All other staff was very helpful and pleasant. I can tick this off my bucket list and visit to Eiffol Tower.

The food was so good, glad we had dinner there, the music during dinner was perfectly lively but not intrusive to conversation. The show itself was amazing! Highly entertaining and the level of talent was incredable. Highly recommend to do in Paris!

If you like Cabarets you will definetly like this one. We purchased the VIP package and had front row seating as well, which was a plus. I am not sure if the seats in the back had the view like the people in the front. I must say I enjoyed the show! Try to get there early because of the line.

Show was fantastic. Tables were very close to each other and cramped. It was expensive at £103. But it was for my mother's birthday so it didn't matter. Beware taxis outside try to rip you off. Always ask for price. Ours said 30 euros before it even set off. Instead of the usual 2.70 start fee. Needless to say we didn't get in it.

We decided against the meal and show option and just went to see the show. We were taken to our seats which happened to be on a table where a couple were already seated eating a romantic meal for two! There were four of us squeezed onto the end of a table sized for four people maximum with this poor couple. We were at the end of a row of tables like this and I felt uneasy that if there were an incident we would be trapped. The show was very enjoyable and at least we can say we have been there and done it.

We did not eat here because we heard the food is a lot of money and not good quality, but we booked tickets for the show. It was so out of date and cheesy! They weren't really dancing at all, the choreography was so simple - I have seen better shows at our local club. However, the3 sight acts were very good. I suggest you use the money you will save by not going on a nice dinner.

My Mom was really excited to go, so my little brother & I took our parents. I paid for the tix which are not inexpensive, but we had fantastic seats & decent service. The show was cheesier than Rockefeller Rockettes, but fantastic for my Mom & Dads enjoyment alone. And honestly, we had so much champagne, my brother & I had a great time too. I'm glad they offer it. There is partial nudity, so not suitable for all parents. lol

No Spoilers Here...Its doesn't matter what you hear, you have to see it to believe it. They have perfected a show that has been recreated by Las Vegas and many shows throughout the world. Buy the champagne bottle option and remember you can order more of anything on or off the menu. Some pieces of advice...Arrive early, wear comfy shoes and bring someone you love as you will me amazed and aroused at the male and female performers and appreciate the discipline it takes to perform the various acts of entertainment. Sidenote avoid the adult club next door as you leave...it is a sham and a rip off it is easy to be drawn in after such a quality show but avoid it at all costs.

The show has topless nudity and for whatever reason I just did not expect this, maybe because I am an America, go figure. If you are looking to go to a strip show, this place would be for you. After watching the movie Moulin Rouge I assumed the show would be more burlesque dancing with less men. A Vegas show has a better variety of acts and performances, there is no need to go for the sentiment of visiting the classic Moulin Rouge. In one part there is a man spitting ping pong balls out of his mouth and into water. He than proceeds to pop the balls in the air and catch them in his mouth. All the other acts were just this dumb except there naked women on stage. The dancing and singing is simply not that good to be honest and I would not recommend spending your time and money on it. I walked out feeling disappointed and grossed out.

Don't visit Paris and miss this show!! 100% worth it, a total experience of two hours of entertainment and fun... Yes, not for kids!!!! But, very clean and wonderful. Please do the champagne package with the entrance for the show..

We bought our VIP tickets well in advance of the show. Probably about 5 months. It was well worth it. We had great seats. The exterior is beautiful the interior is very detailed. No cameras are allowed when entering the theatre. It is a smaller theatre - similar to an underground off broadway theatre size in NYC. The show was tasteful and the show was classic. They had smaller acts in between the main "burlesque" part of the show. Please do not bring your children to the show as there is nudity most of the time. My only complaint is that because there is nudity there are some audience members who sometimes make rude noises to the performers in the middle of the show. There was little respect from the people who were seated next to us.

If you want colour, music, fantastic side acts and song in your Paris experience, go to Moulin Rouge. Don't bother booking in your home country. Our hotel Concierge made the bookings for us and it was cheaper than booking with a travel agent. We had the best seats on the night down the front of the stage and to the right. So much colour and music it is continuous for two hours and every minute is entertaining. The girls, the boys, the costumes did not disappoint. We only went for the show but you can for a bigger cost have dinner as well. The wait staff where friendly and always there if needed to pour drinks or check if you needed anything extra. The Can Can number is brilliant and the extra acts are amazing. This is a MUST SEE if you love musical theatre.

Great one time experience, about 200 euros for 3 course meal + half bottle wine.
Definitely a must do in Paris if you haven't been here before. Definitely wont be doing it again, but great to experience this.

What a night! And worth every penny. I know this is a very expensive way to spend an evening in Paris, but it really is a once in a life time event. My husband and I arrived at 8pm for the 9pm show. We were shown to our table - right at the very front of the stage! We were given our bottle of champagne and there was some pre show entertainment. The table seated 10 (5 couples). The venue is just amazing, plush and rich vibrant colours. During the day the outside looks quite run down and disappointing but once darkness falls and the lights come on it transforms to the iconic Moulin Rouge we see in all the movies and pictures.
The show itself is fabulous. I don’t want to spoil it for anyone going, but prepared to be amazed, wowed and truly entertained from start to finish.
I cannot recommend it highly enough. My husband and I enjoyed meeting the couple sitting next to us. We were probably the last 4 to leave the venue. With it being a Sunday evening, there was no 11pm show that night, so the staff were in no hurry to move us out 😃. All the staff we encountered were lovely.
The Moulin Rouge is a must-see when visiting Paris.

We were so excited to see what this would be....turns out it was an unsophisticated, tacky mess. In one number, there are dancers dressed like pirates, mid-east Aladin types, and I don't even know what. The choreography and production was so lame. If you're used to Any quality theater (Broadway etc..) this will be painful to sit through. Unless you laugh throughout it like we did. There are also a handful of male dancers wearing the cheesiest outfits, we expected them to strip like chip n' dale dancers, but the awful costumes stayed on. They should've kept it vintage. This was just bizarre.

Unless you support sexism or animal cruelty, I can't reccomend this show. Up some peoples street, but failed to meet my expectations. All singing, all dancing and a lot of scantily clad (read: only wearing thongs) women, alongside fully clothed men?? Use of shetland ponies and snakes utterly unnecessary and surprised it is allowed in this day and age! Appreciate it is a French show, but as English guests we could not follow the storyline (if there was one) at all. Expensive tickets, money better spent elsewhere. Highlights: roller skating / dancing duo during set changes, cheap champagne and the lady sat behind us who literally fel0l asleep.

I was so excited to go to there but treated poorly by the usher! I went with my adult daughter and we arrived reasonably early - we were lined up in sections at the back of the theatre waiting to go in. When we finally made it through all the stairs and checks we were assigned an usher to take us to our seats - he directed us to a tiny little table near a big pillar and then after he saw the disappointment in my face quickly turned on his heel huffing and puffing and put us in another obscure location where it was hard to see. I asked if we could sit on a table facing the stage because there were plenty of empty tables in good positions and he replied ‘NOT POSSIBLE’. He then took us to the edge of the room facing away from the stage. It didn’t matter how early we arrived - because we were not a group of four or six, we were just placed to plug gaps in seating on partially full tables! Such a huge disappointment and the show hadn’t even started. When the show did start it was entertaining but the use of ponies was unnecessary and a huge python being forced to stay in water was horrible. I gave the show a 4 but the manners of the usher, the overcrowding, the unnecessary use of animals and the seating is why my overall rating is 1!!!

Given the scale of the show, the history attached to it and the generous portion of alcohol I thought 130 euros was more than a fair price. We went to the nine PM show which was fairly full but we were not exactly packed in as I expected. The three of us purchased tickets giving us each a half bottle of champagne or wine and two of our party selected champagne and the other wine, we got a full bottle of each which was more than enough for a two hour show. No one engaged in a hard sell of any extras, photos, water, programs which I appreciated.

The show is on a scale larges than I expected, during the big production numbers you might have more than 45 dancers on various parts of the stage. That said I found most of the big numbers a bit dated, some reminded me of shows from the 60s and 70s except on a larger scale. The sailor and ship portion seemed pre the 60s and not all that good to boot. I also could have done without the snake in the pool portion of the show. On the other hand the duets were quite good and I don't regret for one moment going to the Moulin Rouge. It's certainly not one of the best shows I've seen, nor nearly the most expensive, but I enjoyed it and want to thank the waiter who as we were leaving offered a bit of history and pointed out some of the art work from about 1897, faded a bit but still there.

It's a lot of show and it's well run. I would suggest the 11 PM show and going during the work week as it was clear to us that had we gone at that hour it likely would not have been the least bit crowded, seemed to us that some of the tables closer to the stage were packed in at the nine PM hour.

You will be sat at a table (as wide as a skateboard) with 4 other strangers cramped in like sardines with the other tables beside you. You sit side on to the stage so your neck will be in agony after about 30 mins, with no room to move your seat to face a better way. I had the view of the back of a 50year old mans head the whole show. I've never been so glad that something came to an end and I could actually stand up. Back and neck killing me. The champagne was like vinegar. The show itself had some good acts, the main parts of the show were OK, not the greatest synchronised dancing I've ever seen but in general it was good.

I went there because it was a "must see" in Paris. However, for the price we pay for the tickets and the treatment and conditions offered - are very bad. The doors open and we are "hoarded" into the theatre. They cram as many people possible to sit at one table. My husband was seated with his back turned to the stage - really not worth the price. The show was good.

Book very early and arrive early on the day as queues are long, campaign included, shows goes on for about 2.5 hrs without interlude. Food can be ordered for the table if arriving and seated early enough. Every table that is located above floor level has a good view due to clever planning. VIP area at the very top.

I have been twice before and took my granddaughter as I knew she would love it as she takes dance in high school. She was totally mesmerized by the whole show and loved all the interludes as well. The costumes were superb and the dancing fantastic. Would go again as it changes every time...

Getting in was not as bad as I thought it would be. We got there 15 minutes before the time, I was concerned we will get bad seats. Luckily we were seated right at the middle, just perfect. The place was packed. Each of us was given one bottle of wine of our choice. The show was enjoyable to the end.

This review likely echos many of the negative ones I have seen online. Upon arrival we lined up and were taken through to the theatre. We were then shoved to a section in the back corner of the room. For that amount of money we paid for tickets, restricted visibility is not expected. Many customers would have purchased tickets for the same amount and received much better seats. In addition to that, we were placed on a platform just above the pathway where the waiters walk through. For the first half an hour of the show, there were many staff members constantly passing through every 5-10 seconds. At one point, 4-5 staffers stopped in front of us to have a conversation during the middle of the show. We were not offered a menu, drink, water, etc the entire time. When we finally asked for a menu, the waiter did not return to accept the order.

The show itself was also of very poor quality. Most of the singing was not live, some performers were not familiar with the routines which caused many pieces to be out of time and look awkward on stage. This occurred throughout the entire duration of the performance. The material was primarily the dancers walking around the stage showcasing their bodies and costumes as opposed to entertaining the crowd. The FAQ section on the website states that the show is “suitable for all ages”, there is no consideration for the many revealing outfits. I did not expect the majority of the show to be topless and am surprised there is no mention of this as a guide for parents looking to take children to the performance.

Another key point of the show which was disgusting was the animal cruelty. The dancer swimming with the snakes, grabbing them violently and flinging them over her head. It was very uncomfortable to watch, especially when snakes should be moved around and treated with caution. Not to mention the many ponies which were costumed and brought onto stage later on in the performance.

The only enjoyable part of the show were the circus acts. I have no doubt that these performers are underpaid for their talent and contribution to the show. That was quality talent unlike the rest of the operation.

The bottom line is that this amount of money spent could have otherwise been used elsewhere on our trip. It is awful to feel so taken advantage of, with the amount of audience members in attendance. There are many more attractions in Paris where this money could have been put to better use. The reason they do not allow filming or photography is because the show is that bad. We have seen the Lido before which was of a much higher quality and standard. Both service and performance wise. Having seen many shows in the past, I was very disappointed by the quality of the very famous Moulin Rouge. Having recently voyaged aboard an MSC cruise ship, the dancers there performed a better rendition of the can-can. It was extremely disappointing for the amount of prestige and history that the brand carries. The crowd did not seem enthused, I feel as though this was the general consensus of the entire audience. DO NOT waste your time and money when there are so many other wonderful things to do in Paris. If you are in the area though, the outside of the building is worth a photo.

Where do I start- it was absolutely terrible! Grumpy ushers at doors, queuing for ages in a horrible warehouse/old stage inside the theatre, rude, military-style cloakroom staff demanding I check a tiny bag no one has ever asked me to check in ten years of travelling (!), seats at right angles to the stage! The staff (especially the cloakroom lady) were some of the rudest, bossiest, most demanding and arrogant I have ever encountered in my life. It didn’t feel like a theatre at all- more like an institution with wannabe prison guards or something. We’re paying customers going to the theatre- not slaves you know. I left the theatre- life’s too short to waste time with such rude companies. The show itself was like some tired old glittered club show. If you want to see this business continuing MANAGEMENT NEEDS TO DO SOMETHING ABOUT THE BOSSY, RUDE, MILITANT STAFF- they’re acting like their on some sort of power trip, not serving someone in a theatre.

I am astounded by this terrible experience especially somewhere that used to be so famous. Someone needs to do something about the attitude of the staff (especially the cloakroom staff)- or this business will fade away. Paying customers aren’t going to stand being treated like that.

It is simply not good enough.

We were very excited to watch a show at The Moulin Rouge, and I've never been left, from a show, feeling so ripped off. It was horrendously dated and not in a vintage way. The dancers were not technically good, esp the boys, they were border line awful, and the lip syncing was a shocker I wasnt ready for and it wasn't a cheap show.

Deflated, sad and lacking creative inspiration!

Don't bother.

The 11pm Friday night show at the Moulin Rouge on October 12 2018 was well attended with folks from all over the France and the World. After mentioning that my wife and I were on our honeymoon, the attendant sat us Center Stage in the back of the theathre, 1 level up from the main floor. The view was perfectly centered our eyes were level with stage. From the moments the lights dimmed to the group serenade at the end of the show there was not one moment that did not captivate us, move us to tears and applause, and completely delighted our senses of sight and sound. The combination of costumes, beautiful bodies, amazing light effects, perfectly choreographed dancing and daring acrobatics, singing and dancing totally mesmerized us from one beginning to end. We left humbled, honored and blessed by the incredible workmanship of over 100 highly skilled and talented artists. Overall this was money very well spent and worth sacrificing something else we might not have done while in Paris. Truly a Bucket List Item ! Go to Moulin Rouge at least once in your life. If already in Paris, DON'T HESITATE.

I was excited to see the Feerie show at the Moulin Rouge, however, was a bit disappointed afterwards.
We were crammed on a tiny table (best suited for 4), with additional 4 people and not enough room to move your seat. We had to grab a waiter, as they shot past, to get a drink and were never asked again for additional drinks.
Some of the dancing was great, but overall, simple and dated.
The costumes, or half costumes(!), were amazing! As were the sets.
There were some acts, that were amazing, but for the price, 3 acts did not justify paying that amount.
It is something you would only see in Paris and it was something I had to do, but be prepared for an average show.

The show uses animals which is not ok- first snakes then baby ponies, so unnecessary and awful
The ponies looked miserable
The show was tacky
The good parts were the supporting acts which were very talented - they were only 3

I read all of the mixed reviews and decided I could just not miss this iconic thing to do in Paris. I was not disappointed. The show at times was cheesy but I would not trade the experience for anything.

I debated this one. The longstanding popularity and the costs of the ticket, not to mention the late hour for the show. . . but there were four of us, and I was out voted. I envisioned some tacky Las Vegas stripper thing, complete with the creepy customers. No, not at all. The show was tasteful, exciting, and very well done. I don't want to tell you, but other reviews mentioned the reptiles, juggling, and humorous parts that made the show much more than a showgirl - stripper thing. Actually the show was very entertaining. The club is nice. We were seated on the back balcony, not the "best seats in the house," and they were fine. Two bottles of champagne being included helped. The audience, like us, were rather clean cut visitors out to have a great night in Paris.
Thank you Moulin Rouge, we did just that -- had a great time!

Hadn't been to a Paris show in years so had our Hotel concierge book the Moulin Rouge late show for us. Best ever show. My partner had never been to Moulin Rouge and he loved it. The dance troupes, the singing and the marvellous acrobats and balancing acts left us in awe. What gorgeous girls and guys, what fabulous and glamorous costumes - the music, dance precision and cheography is world class. What athletes these dancers are and then there are the balancing acts and the girl in the pool with the large reptile-That was amazing . We enjoyed going to the late show after dinner. What a very Parisienne thing to do. Thanks Moulin Rouge .

Due to the world pandemic that is happening at the moment the moulin rouge closed when I was supposed to be going to see the moulin rouge, on March 13th I was promised a refund would be in my bank within a few days, by April it was and they told me I would have to wait until May, got in contact on May and now apparently I have to wait until June ! Surely one member of the accounts team can go to work and issue the refunds that are due !? £120 x 2 tickets is money that is needed at this moment in time.
Canceled,the whole trip was cancelled,so please refund the value of the tickets ,I can not rate the show since we did not see it

We paid about 145 euro etch for tickets on the Moulin Rouge website and arrived early to queue. It was unclear how seats were assigned. I had read it was first-come-first-serve, but we were 45 minutes early and had some of the worst seats in the house (on the very side sitting at a table with two strangers). Better seats were still open when we came in, so I'm not sure if these were VIP or if it's just arbitrary how you are seated. We went to the 9 pm show, and it was only about an hour and a half (there is also an 11 pm show, so they need to get you out and the other guests seated). If tickets had been more reasonably priced, then it might have been worth it just for a cultural experience, but the price-quality ratio didn't come out in favour of this show. First, if you don't speak French, you won't understand any of the comic bits. Second, the dancing is just mediocre. The women seem more chosen for having uniform breast appearance (or I guess it's probably hard to dance with bare breasts?), but I actually wanted to see good dancing (in one number, to give a sense, women just walked miniature ponies around the stage--that's all they did, just walked them around). There was one number with really talented roller skaters that basically carried the show for me. They were the only performers on par with what I was expecting in terms of showcasing talent and riveting the audience. My husband and I were both underwhelmed and left wishing we hadn't spent the money. As we did a search on whether it was worth the money before purchasing, wanted to provide our perspective for anyone else on the fence. If you aren't really excited about it going in, then it probably won't wow you. Oh, and the option to have the champagne on your ticket is a good one if you actually want to drink as it's a lot more expensive in the theatre. I don't think you can get even a single glass of wine for less than 15 euro.

We splurged a little to see the show as VIPs and I can say I was not disappointed. It is nice to be treated like royalty for a night. We completely bypassed the line at the door and were ushered into a salon where we were served champagne while we waited to be seated at a table for two in the balcony. We had superb seats right on the glass so I did not need to crane my neck to see around someone in front of me. Our waiter kept our glasses full, brought us coffee and made sure we were quietly cared for without interrupting the show. The show itself was fantastic. Each scene was a feast for the eyes with colorful costumes, backdrops, lighting, singing and dancing and every time the lights came up it was something new and different. The special acts were fantastic!
I will make one small complaint and word of caution: skip the photographer! A photographer came through before the show started offering to take a photo which we declined and I'm glad we did, she came back through after the show started to sell photo packages to those who had their photo taken, it was a real disruption and I felt bad for folks who had agreed. I feel like you could pick up your photo packages after the show and there's no need to do this type of sales pitch during the performance.

We are a family of 5 from New York. We attended the 11pm show on Thursday. It was full. I booked well in advanced but couple in line next to us said they booked last minute that day. We started lining up around 10:30pm, there was already about 75 people in front of us and about 50 people behind us by the time we got to the theater entrance. Seats are assigned as you come in. I thing any seats are good, its a small theater with good view of the stage. Half a bottle of Champagne per person but my kids requested water and coke. they gave each 2 bottle of coke(per person) and 2 bottles of evan water(per person) in replacement for the Champagne. There was a lot of dancing and singing in French. there are a few songs in English toward the end. Circus acts in between, juggler, roller skating couple, contortionist, lady swimming and a bit of nudity during all the dancing. My 13 year old and 17 year old was a bit uncomfortable with nudity but the show overall was very entertaining.

Show is very repetitive. Felt like I was watching a show put on by a cruise.

Low quality. Fell asleep during the show.

Very touristy!!!!!
Do not spend the money!

We went to the 9pm show with champagne...the way the seats are oriented half of the audience would have their backs to the stage. You can turn the chairs but the tables are pretty close together. Our party of 4 had to share a table of 6. The dancers were ok. The best part was the contortionist.
I have been to many shows in US but can't compare anything with Moulin Rouge Show in Paris, it is different to all shows you might have seen in Vegas.

One for the Bucket list! Spectacular dancing and sheer dynamism. Risqué - not really, just admire the athleticism and costumes. We just had half bottle champagne (with alternative of 2 bottles coke etc for non drinkers. Had to sit on table with others who had eaten earlier, but no problem with view. Must do this!

This show is very fun to watch, we visited on the first night of our trip and were still talking about it a week later. We didn't have dinner, just a bottle of champagne to enjoy during the show. The music and dancing is very entertaining, and there were some great acrobatic type segments of the show that we loved. I have highly recommended this event to my friends!
We had great seats, great service and the show was spectacular. It was the highlight of our Paris visit.

The Moulin Rouge from the outside is very nice lots of people but is so expensive over price. And what makes it worst a person can't even walk on the side road it is totally block off all sides. It is not so big attracting as people say it is

really enjoyed the show at the molin rouge - looking at our holiday photos now & wishing we could have a time machine & be beck there .
pricey but a really great quality show - its a must do if you visit paris - even more so during st valentines week

Hi,
Needed to cancel my attendance for the show due to unforeseen sickness, but no refund and I was charged the full price of the show (2 people).

Due to the riots and strikes in Paris, our transportation was cancelled, and it was nearly impossible, and definitely undesirable to be in Paris. The policy on TripAdvisor says there are no cancellations on this booking, so we decided to follow up for refund after our trip was over (because we had to book an entirely new backup trip while already traveling in another country!). Moulin Rouge refuses to give us a refund for our tickets and TripAdvisor/Viator aren't standing behind their customer. We will avoid using this service at all costs in the future.

Before booking I read the reviews and I normally don't read the full on negative ones, because I think thode people are just negative people. So therefore, we booked the tickets because other than some very negative ones, there were mostly 5-star reviews.
